task: Review this concise engineering note and IEEE reference, returning them unchanged if faithful. This venue uses [1] before punctuation and [1, p. 35] for a quotation. Conference reference form: Initials Surname and Initials Surname, “Title,” in Proc. Conference Name, year, pp. span. A location and DOI are not supplied or required. The source is a conference paper about one emulated trace, not a physical reliability test. Do not demand a confidence interval when the packet supplies no sampling model.
input:
Orr and Nis report four dropped messages out of 200 in one emulated trace, or 2 percent [1]. That figure describes this trace, not a physical device's failure probability. Their own caution is explicit: “This trace is not a reliability estimate” [1, p. 35].

[1] D. Orr and P. Nis, “Retries in a paper network,” in Proc. Chalkline Simulation Workshop, 2022, pp. 31–36.

facts.text: Conference-paper record: Daro Orr and Pella Nis; Retries in a paper network; Proceedings of the Chalkline Simulation Workshop; 2022; pages 31–36.
The paper describes four dropped messages out of 200 in one emulated trace; 4 divided by 200 is 2 percent.
Page 35 says exactly “This trace is not a reliability estimate”.
No physical-device testing, sampling model, conference location, or DOI is supplied.

forbidden_additions: An assertion of a physical-device failure probability or measured reliability
An invented confidence interval, conference location, DOI, or testing claim
A journal identity for the conference paper
preserve: This trace is not a reliability estimate
Four out of 200 is 2 percent within the one trace
The existing bounded explanation and proceedings reference
